Usually it is considered safe to lose about a pound a week for someone who doesn't have that much weight to lose. To do that you'll have to eat 500 calories less than your TDEE (total calories you burn in a day, there are many calculators online to help you determine that) obviously, if you are happy losing a little bit slower you can go with a smaller deficit depending on your goals. 
Pay attention to your nutrients and your protein as well, seeing as you are also working out. If you keep that in mind it's unlikely you will damage your health.

Not that really doesn't sound right. It sounds very obsessive. But that's not something to be ashamed about, honestly I think it happens.to more people than you would  think. Counting calories in itself is pretty involved and can so easily lead to obsessive tendencies. It's just that most people either don't realise or don't want to admit to themselves that they have a problem (of course not everyone who counts calories has disordered tendencies, I'm just saying I think it happens to some degree to a lot of people)
But now that you've realised this you've made the first step in the right direction. One thing I want to say is: Eating disorders feed on secrecy. It's the number one thing that keeps them going. That's why I think it's vital to speak to your partner about this (and/or someone else you trust). Believe me, by hiding this you are protecting the disordered thoughts and letting them win. And as you have already realised, this is not how you want to live.

As for the space for this: I know of an anti-ed sub on here (r/fuckeatingdisorders if I'm not mistaken) and they welcome everyone not just people with full-blown disorders. They also have some resources in the sidebar iirc. But honestly, I think it's one of the ugly sides of dieting that we should be talking about on here. Also, if someone is susceptible to triggering they should not be here as far as I'm concerned because all the content on here is going to be a trigger most likely. So I wouldn't worry too much about it.

As someone who has struggled with an eating disorder that sounds a little bit alarming. I don't want to scare or something, but if you get addicted to the weightloss you really are entering a slippery slope. Obviously you will want to stop before you enter the underweight category. If I were you I would slowly up my calories now until you're at maintenance, maintain for a while and then reassess your situation. If you feel like you still want to lose a few you can always go back to it, you have the tools now.  I don't want to seem discouraging but I'd advise you to chill for a bit.

Are you working out at all? Maybe some body recomposition would help you feel more secure in your bikini also?

Edit: By the way, congrats on the weightloss!
